turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, Miss Havisham, but I don't know if Estella is free to come in just now, she's always with you and it seems like you want me to play, but I'd rather not disturb her if she's busy

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will call Estella, now. I will not be ignored.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I was afraid, Miss Havisham, that I might be disturbing her, and I wouldn't want to do that if she's occupied, but if you really wish her to come, I'll call her, I suppose

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, I suppose, does not have a busy schedule like ordinary people. Bring her to me at once, I have no patience for your excuses.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure, Miss Havisham, if I should call Estella when you're in one of these... moods, and I fear she might not come, if she knows you're not pleased with me

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I warn you, Pip, do not attempt to defy me or you will regret it. I will not be disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't wish to displease you, Miss Havisham, but I'm not sure it's right to call Estella when she might be... um, resting or engaged in some other quiet activity

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be deterred by your excuses, Pip. I demand to see Estella at once, and I will not be disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't want to trouble Estella, Miss Havisham, and I'm not sure she'd want to come if she knows you're in a hurry, it might make her uncomfortable

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will call for Estella at once, and you will make certain she knows that I await her in the parlour. I will not be disobeyed, Pip.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know if Estella is in a state to be disturbed, Miss Havisham, and I wouldn't want to cause her any distress

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are a foolish boy, Pip, to think that Estella requires rest or quiet, when she was designed to be a cold and distant thing, a heartbreak waiting to happen, and I will not be thwarted in my plans.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't want to cause any more trouble, Miss Havisham, and I'm not sure I'm the right person to fetch Estella, maybe it would be better if you asked one of the servants to go?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my authority, Pip, and suggest that I rely on the servants to carry out my wishes? I will not be disobeyed, and you will fetch Estella at once.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I'm not sure I can fetch Estella, Miss Havisham, I'm not familiar with your plans and I don't want to cause any more trouble, perhaps you could explain what you wish me to do?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will do as I say, Pip, because I have a purpose for you to serve, and you will not disappoint me, not yet, at least.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I understand what you mean, Miss Havisham, and I don't want to do anything that might be wrong, could you please explain what you need me to do?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are to play cards with me, Pip, and I insist that you do not leave my side until we have finished the game. I have a special deck, one that I have not used in years, and it is said to bring good fortune to those who play with me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I'm comfortable playing cards with you, Miss Havisham, I've never played cards before and I don't want to make a mistake and lose your favor

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play cards with me, Pip, and you will not waste my time with your excuses and doubts. I have been waiting for someone to play with for a very long time, and I will not be disappointed now.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
